concepts.name: Establishment and Statutory Mandate of EXIM Bank of India
key_dimensions: Founded under the Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981 — NOT under Companies Act (common trap)
Commenced operations on January 1, 1982, replacing the International Finance wing of IDBI
Principal financial institution (not just a commercial bank) for coordinating working of institutions engaged in financing exports/imports
Wholly owned by Government of India — distinction from ECGC which is also GoI-owned but serves insurance function

concepts.name: EXIM Bank vs. ECGC: Functional and Structural Distinctions
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank: financing/lending institution; ECGC: export credit insurance/guarantee body — frequently confused in MCQs
ECGC operates under Ministry of Commerce; EXIM Bank under Ministry of Finance — different administrative oversight
ECGC covers credit risk; EXIM Bank provides direct loans, guarantees, and lines of credit
Both are GoI-owned but serve complementary, non-overlapping roles in export promotion ecosystem

concepts.name: Lines of Credit (LoC) Mechanism of EXIM Bank
key_dimensions: LoC is a financing mechanism where EXIM Bank extends credit to overseas entities/governments to facilitate Indian exports — key instrument of economic diplomacy
Difference between LoC and direct loan: LoC benefits recipient country's buyers, not Indian exporters directly
India's LoCs under Indian Development and Economic Assistance Scheme (IDEAS) — link to Ministry of External Affairs
EXIM Bank as implementing agency for government-to-government LoCs: trap point — LoCs are sovereign commitments, not EXIM Bank's own risk

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Role in South-South Cooperation and Development Finance
key_dimensions: Extends concessional LoCs to African, Asian, and Latin American nations — instrument of India's soft power
Distinction between concessional LoC (subsidized rate, often for development projects) vs. commercial LoC
EXIM Bank as India's nodal agency for implementing LoCs under GoI's foreign policy — not ADB or World Bank
Overlap trap: Development Finance Institution (DFI) role vs. NaBFID (recently created DFI for domestic infrastructure)

concepts.name: Buyer's Credit vs. Supplier's Credit: EXIM Bank Instruments
key_dimensions: Buyer's Credit: credit extended to foreign buyer to purchase Indian goods — demand-side financing
Supplier's Credit: credit extended to Indian exporter who in turn offers deferred payment terms to buyer — supply-side financing
UPSC trap: In Buyer's Credit, the overseas buyer is the borrower; in Supplier's Credit, the Indian exporter is the borrower
Both mechanisms boost Indian exports but differ in who bears credit risk and who is the primary obligor

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Equity Participation and Overseas Investment Finance
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank can finance Indian companies' overseas direct investments — unique among Indian financial institutions
Supports joint ventures and wholly owned subsidiaries abroad — promotes Indian MNCs
Distinction: EXIM Bank finances outward FDI; it does NOT regulate FDI (RBI/FEMA does that)
Overseas investment finance as a tool to create a 'production base abroad' for re-export — concept of export platform investment

concepts.name: EXIM Bank and Project Exports: Turnkey and Construction Contracts
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank specifically supports 'project exports' — engineering, construction, turnkey projects executed abroad by Indian firms
Project Exports Promotion Council (PEPC) works alongside EXIM Bank — distinction of roles (PEPC: promotional body; EXIM Bank: financier)
Deferred payment terms for project exports require EXIM Bank guarantees — critical for competitive bidding in global tenders
UPSC angle: Project exports are categorized differently from merchandise exports under BoP and DGFT statistics

concepts.name: Guarantee Schemes Offered by EXIM Bank
key_dimensions: Types: Bid Bond Guarantee, Performance Guarantee, Advance Payment Guarantee, Retention Money Guarantee
Distinction trap: EXIM Bank guarantees cover contractual performance risk; ECGC covers commercial and political credit risk
Guarantees enable Indian exporters to participate in overseas tenders without locking up capital
EXIM Bank guarantee ≠ ECGC guarantee: EXIM Bank guarantee is issued to the overseas buyer/project authority; ECGC guarantee is issued to Indian commercial banks

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Role in Financing MSMEs and Cluster Development
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank extends credit to export-oriented MSMEs directly and through partner banks (two-step lending)
Distinction: Two-step lending (via banks) vs. direct lending to exporters — EXIM Bank is not a retail bank
Export marketing finance for MSMEs — covers overseas marketing expenses, a lesser-known product
UPSC trap: SIDBI is the principal institution for MSME financing broadly; EXIM Bank's MSME role is specifically export-linked

concepts.name: EXIM Bank and the National Export Insurance Account (NEIA)
key_dimensions: NEIA is a Trust managed by EXIM Bank to support project exports to difficult/high-risk markets where ECGC cover is unavailable
Funded by Government of India grants — sovereign backing distinguishes NEIA from commercial insurance
EXIM Bank as trustee-manager of NEIA, not as insurer — important functional distinction
NEIA fills the gap between commercial risk appetite and strategic export promotion goals — geopolitical dimension

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Borrowing and Resource Mobilization
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank raises resources through bonds, term loans, and external commercial borrowings (ECBs) — NOT through public deposits (unlike commercial banks)
Issues bonds in international capital markets (e.g., Green Bonds, Masala Bonds) — foreign currency resource mobilization
Government of India guarantee on EXIM Bank borrowings — sovereign backing lowers cost of funds
Trap: EXIM Bank is NOT regulated by RBI for prudential norms in the same way as commercial banks — it is under a separate statute

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Governance Structure and Capital Base
key_dimensions: Board of Directors includes RBI Governor (or nominee), Finance Secretary, Commerce Secretary — inter-ministerial coordination built into structure
Authorized capital and paid-up capital structure under the 1981 Act — periodically enhanced by Parliament
Wholly owned by GoI: no private shareholding (unlike IDBI which was partially divested)
CMD vs. MD nomenclature: headed by Managing Director — not Chairman-cum-MD (common confusion with PSBs)

concepts.name: EXIM Bank in the Context of India's Foreign Trade Policy (FTP)
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank operationalizes financial aspects of FTP; DGFT operationalizes regulatory/procedural aspects — clear division
FTP 2023: EXIM Bank's role in supporting 'Towns of Export Excellence' and MSME export clusters
EXIM Bank data and research inputs feed into Annual Report on Indian Export Competitiveness
Trap: EXIM Bank does NOT grant export incentives (MEIS/RoDTEP) — those are DGFT/Ministry of Commerce instruments

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Research and Advisory Functions
key_dimensions: Publishes Working Papers, Occasional Papers on trade competitiveness, BoP, and sectoral export potential
Conducts 'Export Potential Index' studies — identifies districts/states with untapped export potential
Advisory services to exporters on market entry, trade finance structuring — beyond pure lending mandate
Distinction: EXIM Bank research is trade-finance focused; FICCI/CII research is industry-advocacy focused; IIFT research is academic

concepts.name: EXIM Bank vs. World Bank/ADB/New Development Bank: Multilateral vs. Bilateral DFI
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank is a bilateral institution (India-centric); MDBs are multilateral — fundamentally different governance
India is a member/shareholder of ADB, World Bank, NDB — these bodies lend TO India; EXIM Bank lends FROM India to others
NDB (BRICS Bank) and AIIB are multilateral; EXIM Bank of India, US EXIM Bank, China EXIM Bank are national bilateral institutions
UPSC trap: Differentiating between NDB, AIIB, and India's EXIM Bank in questions about development finance and LoCs

concepts.name: Technology and Innovation Finance: EXIM Bank's Emerging Role
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank finances export of technology-intensive goods and services (IT, pharma, defence exports)
Defence exports: EXIM Bank provides LoCs to friendly foreign nations for purchase of Indian defence equipment — link to 'Make in India' and Atmanirbhar Bharat
Distinction: Defence LoCs are politically sensitive sovereign decisions; EXIM Bank is the financial execution arm, not the decision-making body
Green/Sustainable Finance: EXIM Bank's Green Bond issuances to fund climate-aligned export projects

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Relationship with RBI and Monetary Policy Transmission
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank is a notified All India Financial Institution (AIFI) — regulated by RBI under specific provisions, not as a Scheduled Commercial Bank
Eligible for refinance from RBI — but this is exceptional, unlike commercial banks accessing LAF daily
EXIM Bank's interest rates are market-linked but influenced by GoI interest equalization scheme — subsidy element in export credit
Trap: Interest Equalization Scheme (IES) subvention is routed through RBI to banks and EXIM Bank — GoI pays the differential, not RBI

concepts.name: Interest Equalization Scheme (IES) and Export Credit Subsidization
key_dimensions: IES provides interest subvention on pre and post-shipment rupee export credit — reduces cost of credit for exporters
EXIM Bank and commercial banks both eligible for IES benefits — EXIM Bank is not the sole beneficiary
Scheme periodically renewed (not permanent) — UPSC may test on current validity and recent amendments
Sectors covered under higher subvention rate (MSME manufacturers) vs. merchant exporters — differential treatment is examinable

concepts.name: EXIM Bank's Role in Regional Integration: SAARC, ASEAN, and Africa
key_dimensions: LoCs to SAARC neighbours (Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Maldives) — instrument of India's 'Neighbourhood First' policy
Africa: India's LoC commitments under India-Africa Forum Summits (IAFS) — EXIM Bank as implementing agency
Distinction between LoC (tied to Indian goods/services) and untied aid (no such restriction) — LoCs have local cost financing limits
UPSC trap: LoCs are NOT ODA (Official Development Assistance) in the OECD-DAC definition — they are concessional loans, not grants

concepts.name: EXIM Bank and Special Economic Zones (SEZs) / Export Promotion Zones
key_dimensions: EXIM Bank provides project finance for setting up SEZ infrastructure — distinct from financing SEZ units' exports
Distinction: EXIM Bank finances SEZ developers AND SEZ units; SEZ Act administered by DGFT/Ministry of Commerce
Trap: EXIM Bank is not the regulator of SEZs — it is purely a financier; Board of Approval (BoA) under MoC is the regulator
Recent relevance: SEZ Amendment Act 2023 (DESH Bill proposals) and implications for export finance architecture
